title: Do Prediction Markets Forecast Cryptocurrency Volatility? Evidence from Kalshi Macro Contracts
hypothesis: Daily absolute volume-weighted probability changes in Kalshi macro prediction markets forecast 5-day ahead cryptocurrency realized volatility beyond HAR and market controls
data_sources: Kalshi public API daily closing price, volume, open interest for 10 contract series January 2023 to March 2026
CoinGecko daily closing prices for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Cardano, Avalanche, Chainlink January 2023 to March 2026
CBOE VIX close, DXY index daily return, S&P 500 daily return, Fed Funds futures implied rate, 10Y Treasury return, Deribit DVOL
sample: Merged dataset January 2023 to March 2026 N=1,183 calendar days excluding weekends/US holidays (approx 30% dropped). Effective estimation sample after lagging and matching varies 193-569. Descriptive N=1,178 per crypto. In-sample Bitcoin Fed-dovish N=318. In-sample CPI N=264. Non-overlapping windows N=64 BTC N=54 LINK. Out-of-sample expanding window initial 120 obs, Noos 144-269 per pair.
method: 1. Collect Kalshi series s: KXFED, KXCPI, KXCPICORE, KXGDP, KXU3, KXPCECORE, KXRECSSNBER, KXACPI, KXRATECUT, KXUSNFP via public API from 2023-Q1

2. Construct volume-weighted probability change per Eq1: Delta_vw_s,t = sum_j V_j,t * Delta p_j,t / sum_j V_j,t over active contracts J_s; signal = |Delta_vw_s,t|; also directional Fed-dovish = -Delta_vw_KXFED,t, CPI/NFP directionals; alternatives: 5-day EMA lagged, cross-sectional composite average absolute signal
3. Exclude KXRATECUT (28 obs) and KXUSNFP (0) for insufficient coverage; keep 8 series

4. Crypto returns: r_a,t = ln(P_a,t/P_a,t-1) from CoinGecko midnight-UTC close; dependent var Eq2: RVol_a,t^{h=5} = sqrt(252)* sigma_hat(r_a,t+1...r_a,t+5) sample sd; alternative |r_a,t+1| for non-overlapping, log(RVol+0.001), GARCH(1,1) conditional var, 21-day RVol
5. Timing alignment: Kalshi 4pm ET, VIX/SP500/DXY 4pm ET, crypto midnight-UTC (7pm ET) same calendar date; signal lagged one day Kalshi_{s,t-1} with minimum ~21h gap before forecast window t+1:t+5
6. HAR benchmark M1: RVol^{h=5}= alpha + beta1|r_{t-1}| + beta2 mean|r|^{(5)}_{t-1} + beta3 mean|r|^{(20)}_{t-1} + eps [Corsi 2009]
7. M2 adds Ctrl_t = (VIX_t, r_DXY,t, r_SP500,t)'; M3 adds delta*Kalshi_{s,t-1}
8. Inference: Newey-West HAC 5 lags for overlapping h=5; HC3 for non-overlapping; horizon profile h=1,3,5,10 with HAC lags=min(h,5); moving-block bootstrap block length 5 with 2,000 resamples
9. Multiple testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q=0.05 across 60 signal-by-asset M3 specifications
10. Out-of-sample: expanding window initial 120 days; compute MSFE ratio M3/M2, OOS R2 vs expanding mean, Clark-West f_t = e_b^2 - [e_a^2-(yhat_b-yhat_a)^2] one-sided t-test

11. Robustness: orthogonalization projection on Fed Funds implied change, |change|, VIX, DXY, SP500 (Fed) and 10Y Treasury return, VIX, DXY, SP500 (CPI); baseline comparison M_FF, M_UST, joint with Kalshi; joint with DVOL; lead-lag t-1 vs t+1 placebo; release-window dummy +-3d around BLS CPI and non-release subsample; alternative vol measures
12. CSSED = sum_t (e_b,t^2 - e_a,t^2) plotted per best signal
